summary: Iteration 2 re-derives the case blind: no iteration-1 table, candidate gene or rank was read to build this step, and the gate that checks that (`mva-science check --blind`) is enforced by tooling, not by promise. Step 1 ranks every HPO-curated gene against the proband's 7 clinical terms (plus an 8th, parental-history term) with two independent rankers, and turns the top 300 plus a mechanism-term carve-out into a 404-gene target set with a 396-gene shape-matched decoy set alongside it as a null. Four claims were pre-registered and all four are resolved: only H013 (a recessive chromosome-instability gene is in the set) held. Held-out recall@300 was measured twice — once on a 200-disease sample (0.360) and once, after entry 091 removed the sampling, on the full population of 3,240 eligible diseases (0.335, tighter interval) — and both land far under the 0.90 the step needed to call this set complete coverage.
why: A genome has about 20,000 protein-coding genes and reading two raw datasets (85 GB of reads, a VCF) against all of them is the expensive path. The clinical dataset — 8 HPO terms — is cheap to query first, so the natural move is to let symptoms alone propose a shortlist before opening any DNA. But a shortlist is only useful if its miss rate is known, so H012 measured it rather than assumed it. Without that measurement, step 2 would have baited only the top 300 genes believing that was enough, and a true answer sitting at rank 1,500 would have silently vanished. Measuring recall first — and finding it low — is what turns the target set from an unstated assumption into a stated, quantified enrichment, and is what forces step 4 to exist as a genome-wide safety net that reads every gene in the VCF with no target-set filter at all.
verdict: H012 (recall@300 ≥ 0.90) is refuted: 0.360 [0.295, 0.420] on 200 diseases, confirmed at 0.335 [0.318, 0.350] on the full 3,240-disease population in entry 091 — slightly worse, not better, and the register verdict does not change. H013 (a recessive chromosome-instability gene is in the target set) is supported: 33 such genes are present, though the mechanism-term rule guarantees this close to true by construction, so it is reported as a sanity check, not a discovery. H014 (the two rankers agree on ≥ 50% of their top 300) is refuted at 32.3% overlap. H015 (fewer than 20% of protein-coding genes are uncurated) is refuted: 73.6% of protein-coding genes carry no HPO curation at all and are invisible to this method regardless of symptoms. Decision recorded: the target set stays at N=300 and is described everywhere as an enrichment, never as coverage.

inherits.what: Nothing from a prior iteration-2 step — this is the entry point of the blind re-derivation. It reads only the clinical HPO terms and public reference data (the HPO ontology release, the curation corpus, Ensembl gene models); no genomic file of this child other than the public reference gene model is touched, which is what keeps the blind gate green.

hands_to.what: The 404-row tiered target set and the 396-row decoy set become step 2's bait design (core ±50kb, net ±2kb padding) and its statistical null (H020 asks whether decoys yield fewer biallelic candidates than targets). Step 2 also inherits the load-bearing caveat verbatim: a gene absent from this set is not excluded, only unbaited — which is why step 4 exists as a genome-wide check that never consults this list.

figures.name: recall-at-n.png
figures.reads: Held-out recall on the y-axis against list length N on the x-axis, drawn from the recall curve at N = 1, 10, 50, 300, 1000; N=300 is marked, along with the 0.90 prediction line H012 was tested against.
figures.means: Evidence that H012 fails by a wide margin: recall@300 is 0.360 (200-disease sample) / 0.335 (full population), not 0.90. The curve flattens rather than approaching 1.0 — recall@1000 is only 0.565 (sample) / 0.508 (full population) — which is the basis for the decision that raising N further is not worth the bait cost.

figures.name: target-tiers.png
figures.reads: Composition of the 404-row target set by tier: `core` (62, top 50 by symptom score plus mechanism-term genes scoring inside it), `net` (272, ranks 51–300), `mechanism-term` (70, admitted by annotation regardless of rank).
figures.means: Shows how much of the target set earned its place by symptom score (353 of 404) versus by the mechanism-term carve-out alone (51) — the carve-out is what makes H013 close to true by construction and why that verdict is reported as a sanity check rather than a finding.

figures.name: ranker-overlap.png
figures.reads: Overlap between Phen2Gene's and Monarch semsim's top-300 gene lists, plotted against the 50% agreement H014 predicted.
figures.means: Evidence that H014 is refuted: only 32.3% overlap (97 of 300 genes), far short of the predicted 50%, meaning the two independent phenotype rankers substantially disagree on which genes the symptoms implicate — a reason to treat any single ranker's output as one opinion, not ground truth.

figures.name: curation-coverage.png
figures.reads: Share of protein-coding genes with any HPO curation at all versus those with none, out of 19,723 protein-coding genes.
figures.means: Evidence that H015 is refuted: 73.6% of protein-coding genes (14,523 of 19,723) have zero HPO curation, so a phenotype-only ranker cannot place them at any rank — this is the single largest reason recall@300 cannot reach 0.90 and the strongest argument for calling the target set an enrichment rather than coverage.

figures.name: index.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet combining the four static figures above (recall-at-n, target-tiers, ranker-overlap, curation-coverage) with hover tooltips over each chart.
figures.means: Same evidence as the four figures, in a form that lets a reader inspect exact values per point/bar rather than reading them off a static image.
